turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Right, come through. Sorry, the corridor fan is rattling like anything today.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Ya, I can't hear myself think with that noise. It's ok, I won't sit long, this is nothing much.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): Let me take the readings first. Blood pressure is one oh nine over seventy-seven. Pulse seventy-six. Temperature thirty-six point seven.
[SEG0004] person_1 (NURSE): Oxygen is ninety-eight percent. Breathing sixteen a minute. Weight is sixty-two kilos today.
[SEG0005] person_1 (NURSE): Last time in March you were sixty-eight. Your last pressure was one-forty over eighty-eight.
[SEG0006] person_1 (NURSE): Wait, err, I read the pulse wrong. It is seventy-eight, not seventy-six.
[SEG0007] person_3 (DOCTOR): Thanks. Have a seat. What brought you today?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Umm, it's the sneezing and the running nose, every spring only. I have overdone it in the garden again, that's all.
[SEG0009] person_3 (DOCTOR): Every spring. This spell, how long has it been?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Two three weeks. I can't tell you the exact day, sometime early April maybe. Mild only, my wife forced me to come.
[SEG0011] person_3 (DOCTOR): Even if it feels small, how does a day actually go?

[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): These two three weeks it's sneezing in bouts, worse if I have been in the garden, nose running like a tap that won't shut. Every spring the same story. Mornings I get a frog in my throat. Eyes itch a bit, all mild only.
[SEG0013] person_3 (DOCTOR): The eyes. Are they watering as well as itching?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose. Sometimes, not really.
[SEG0015] person_3 (DOCTOR): Does it spoil your sleep at night?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose, sometimes not really.
[SEG0017] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any wheeze, any whistling sound in the chest?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No wheeze. Chest is perfectly fine.
[SEG0019] person_3 (DOCTOR): And cough, shortness of breath, or fever with this?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): No cough, no breathing problem, no fever. I am telling you it's a small thing.
[SEG0021] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any tablets you are already on for it?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): Cetrizine, ten mg. They told me once a day by mouth. I take it sometimes only, when the sneezing is too much, not daily.
[SEG0023] person_3 (DOCTOR): So daily was the advice and sometimes is what happens. Any other medicine, and any allergies to tablets or anything else?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): No other tablets. No allergies. My sister is allergic to dust, that is her problem, not mine.
[SEG0025] person_3 (DOCTOR): Noted. What work do you do, any smoking, who is at home?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): Accounts job, sitting only. I never smoked. A flat with my wife and two kids, and a bit of Sunday gardening.
[SEG0027] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any asthma or eczema before, or any surgery?
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): No asthma, no eczema. No operation ever. Healthy only, what to do.
[SEG0029] person_3 (DOCTOR): Nasal lining is pale and a little boggy. Eyes are mildly red. Chest is clear, no wheeze when I listen.
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): See, nothing. Some afternoons I feel like a wet rag, but that is just the heat, not this nose thing.
[SEG0031] person_3 (DOCTOR): You're putting that down to the heat. Are your feet numb at all, or was the chair just uncomfortable?
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): My feet feel dead in that waiting chair only. I walk two steps and it's gone. Forget it.

[SEG0033] person_3 (DOCTOR): I won't chase the feet or the heat. About two to three weeks of sneezing, runny nose, itchy eyes and morning throat irritation, the same every spring. No wheeze, no cough and no fever, and the cetirizine ten mg was meant once a day but taken only sometimes. No allergies yourself, your sister has the dust allergy, and you don't smoke, is that fair?
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): Ya, that's correct. Don't make it a big case, doctor.

[SEG0035] person_3 (DOCTOR): I am not going to call this asthma, the chest doesn't support that. My working impression is seasonal allergic rhinitis, though it could also be simple irritant rhinitis from the garden dust and pollen. I can't separate those two fully today. I'm not waiting to see what the tests say, so no bloods and no scans.

[SEG0036] person_3 (DOCTOR): We'll stop the cetrizine ten mg tablet by mouth from today. For the sneezing and the runny nose I'm changing you to fexofenadine, one hundred and eighty mg, one tablet by mouth once a day, right through this season.
[SEG0037] person_3 (DOCTOR): And for the itchy eyes, olopatadin drops, zero point one percent, one drop in each eye twice a day.
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): Fexo is fine. Drops also if you insist. Uh, I will forget the night one, I know myself.

[SEG0039] person_3 (DOCTOR): Put a phone reminder morning and night so the drops actually get used. Don't take cetirizine on top of the new tablet. Windows shut on heavy pollen days, a saline rinse if the nose is pouring, and a mask when you garden.
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): Ok ok. So I come only if it gets worse, or what?

[SEG0041] person_3 (DOCTOR): Come back in four weeks, that visit is booked with me, even if you still think it is nothing. If you start wheezing or the eyes swell, come sooner and don't wait the four weeks.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): Four weeks, fine. I'll tell my wife you people worry too much.
[SEG0043] person_1 (NURSE): I'll hold the four-week slot at the desk. Collect the prescription on the way out.

spec.situation: Sneezing, itchy eyes and runny nose every spring; takes cetirizine 'sometimes'; sister is allergic to dust; no wheeze; doctor changes antihistamine and adds eye drops.

traps.happens: The patient describes things in colourful or sentence-like speech ('I've overdone it', 'I can't hear myself think', 'a frog in my throat', 'my feet feel dead', 'I feel like a wet rag').
traps.label_rule: Every symptom name is a short clinical noun phrase of 1 to 5 words ('voice fatigue', 'numbness in both feet', 'tiredness'), never a full sentence, never starting with I/we/my. Pure idioms that are not symptoms ('I can't hear myself think' said about classroom noise) are NOT symptoms. The patient's own words stay in the cited turn, not in the name.

traps.happens: The nurse reads vital signs aloud in spoken words ('one oh nine over seventy-seven', 'thirty-eight point three') and also gives a PRIOR value ('last time in March you were sixty-eight', 'your last pressure was one-forty'). Someone may also correct a reading.
traps.label_rule: vital_signs hold only the CURRENT measured values, written normally (109/77, 38.3, 52 kg). The prior value is NOT a vital sign; it is recorded in the weight/BP entry's own notes only if the schema allows, otherwise omitted. Every number must be exactly as said; never invent or round a value that was not said.

features: ambiguous_answer: an answer that sounds like yes but is really 'maybe' ('mm, I suppose', 'sometimes, not really'); recorded with uncertainty or not at all, never as a firm fact.

doctor_thinks_aloud: the doctor lists possible causes or says what they will not conclude yet. Only record a clinical assessment if the doctor actually states a leading or differential impression; 'let's see what the tests say' is not an assessment.

bad.reason: Feet numbness with sitting relieved by walking is stated, but transcript does not say both feet or clearly current ongoing symptom.
bad.text: numbness in both feet (category=neurological, status=present, temporality=current, body_site=both feet, aggravating_factors=sitting, relieving_factors=walking, reported_by=patient, certainty=certain)

bad.reason: Drug, dose, route, advice, and discontinuation are stated, but indication was for 'it' not specifically sneezing alone.
bad.text: cetirizine (dose=10 mg, route=oral, frequency=once daily, indication=sneezing, status=discontinued, reported_by=patient)

omissions.text: Watery eyes were asked about and the patient said only sometimes/not really, indicating watering is minimal or inconsistent rather than clearly present.
Sleep disturbance was asked about and the patient gave an equivocal answer: sometimes, not really.
Cetirizine 10 mg by mouth was taken only sometimes/when sneezing is too much, not daily; the medication entry records once daily without the PRN/intermittent actual use detail.
Chest examination was clear, not just no wheeze on auscultation.
The doctor explicitly stated they were not calling this asthma because the chest exam did not support it.
The doctor stated no blood tests and no scans were planned.
The doctor specifically instructed not to take cetirizine on top of the new tablet (fexofenadine).
